subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — Hosted API quickstart & rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API eval - quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really enjoyed learning about Acme's use cases for summarization and embeddings. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Hosted API to power in-product summarization and similarity search for customer support tickets.
- Key constraints: low-latency inference, ability to run embeddings at scale, and no immediate requirement for on-prem.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (quick guidance)
- Hosted API: fastest way to get started (no infra), predictable onboarding, built-in model catalog, and streaming/chat support. Good fit for PoC and early production if you don't need strict VPC or on-prem isolation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools when you need predictable high-throughput (steady QPS > ~50) or heavy token budgets; comes with SLA.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): for regulated workloads or strict data residency/compliance needs.

Quickstart (Hosted API) — what I recommend for the first eval
1) Create an API key in the Console (I can provision a trial key for you).
2) Try this curl to validate connectivity:

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: We had five customer complaints about login failures."}]}'

3) SDK: pip install redwood-inference and use the quick example in the attached quickstart.

Rate limits & quotas (Hosted API) — default guidance
- Default per-key rate: 60 requests per minute (RPM) with burst capacity up to 200 RPM.
- Token throughput: default limits around 300k tokens/min for trial keys; can be increased for production tiers.
- We can request a temporary rate increase for spike testing.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (contains sample code and environment setup). Also attached a sample-integration.zip with a simple Flask example.

Next steps
- Can you confirm expected steady QPS and peak QPS for your evaluation? (helps us advise whether Hosted is sufficient or if Dedicated trial makes sense).
- I can provision a trial API key and temporary rate bump for a 2-week eval. Would Monday 4/14 at 10am PT work for a follow-up to review metrics?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — great demo. A few clarifications from our side:

- Expected load for the eval: steady ~3-5 QPS for chat/generation and embeddings. We do have burst windows during business hours up to ~20 QPS.
- Latency target: 200ms p95 would be ideal for chat flows; embeddings can be a bit higher.
- Data residency: US only is fine for now. We are not yet ready for on-prem.
- Auth/security: standard API keys are OK for the PoC; for production we may need KMS integration and log/audit access.

Could you confirm:
1) Whether the default rate limits you mentioned support 20 QPS bursts?
2) If we need to test higher sustained throughput later, what thresholds tend to push customers toward Dedicated?

Yes to 4/14 at 10am PT — we'll take the trial key and run some smoke tests beforehand.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Senior Product Manager
Acme Analytics

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API eval - quickstart & rate limits

Hi Alex — looping in a couple technical details that help with testing and scale planning.

Rate limits
- 60 RPM is a conservative default for trial keys (which maps to ~1 req/sec). Bursts to 200 RPM cover short spikes. For your stated 20 QPS burst we should request a temporary increase to the trial key (we can provision 300 RPM burst for the window).

When to consider Dedicated
- Typical triggers: steady sustained QPS above ~50, sustained token throughput requirements that cause throttling, or when you need dedicated GPU isolation for latency SLOs. Dedicated gives predictable p95 latency and higher concurrency.

Hosted API endpoints (examples)
- Chat/generation: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
- Completions: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Embeddings: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Sample Node snippet (quick test):

  const Redwood = require('redwood-inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize this ticket...' }] });

Data retention & security
- Hosted API: by default logs are retained for 30 days and can be disabled per contract. We support KMS integrations for key management on Dedicated/Private tiers.

I'll provision a trial key with a temporary RPM bump for your PoC and share the creds via the Console link. If you want to simulate higher sustained throughput we can also spin up a Dedicated trial for a short period.

Attaching: sample-integration.zip (Flask + test harness), and the quickstart PDF Marissa mentioned.

Cheers,

Solutions Engineer
